note: styled drops the stack's fill opacity on the CPU backend, so a faded layer draws at full strength, caught by CPUStyleTests.fillOpacityKept
styled maps every entry to Normal on the CPU backend, so a Multiply shadow or Screen glow blends wrong, caught by CPUStyleTests.everyOpEqualsTheDirectCall
replacement: try derived(s, .style) { try $0.styled(LayerStyleStack(entries: stack.entries.map { StyleEntry(op: $0.op, opacity: $0.opacity, isEnabled: $0.isEnabled) }, fillOpacity: stack.fillOpacity)) }

note: the parity harness renders a style sample with every entry at opacity 1, so a backend is checked against the wrong stack, caught by CPUGoldenTests.cpuReproducesGoldenWithZeroDelta
anchor: case .styled(let stack): out = try backend.styled(s, stack)
replacement: case .styled(let stack): out = try backend.styled(s, LayerStyleStack(entries: stack.entries.map { var e = $0; e.opacity = 1; return e }, fillOpacity: stack.fillOpacity))
